summary: A new day in the app starts at midnight, on your own clock.
notes: New cards for today come back at midnight, not 24 hours after you learned the last ones. Words you learned late in the evening no longer use up the next morning's.
Your streak, today's reviews and times like “tomorrow 06:00” follow the clock on your phone too.

summary: On an iPad held sideways, your decks are on the left and the deck you are in is on the right.
notes: With the iPad sideways, the tabs and your decks are in a list on the left. Tap a deck there to open it straight away, without going back.
A deck of yours shows how to practise on the left and its cards on the right, and each side scrolls on its own.
Turn the iPad upright and it is the page you know, with the same deck still open.

summary: On an iPad the app uses the whole screen: the card is big, and the pages are wider.
notes: When you practise on an iPad, the card is a large card like in Noji, with Again, Hard, Good and Easy in one row under it.
With the iPad sideways, Pick the meaning shows its four answers in two columns.
A deck's page is wider, with the cards for today and How long side by side.
On an iPhone nothing changes.

summary: A card you write can have a real recording, if Kaishi has the word.
notes: While you type the Japanese, the app shows the Kaishi word that is exactly what you typed, with its English meaning. Tap ♪ to hear it, and Use to give your card its recording.
Only take it if it means your German: “kiku” can be to hear, to ask or to be effective.
If you change the Japanese of a card later, a recording of the old word is taken off, so a card never says the wrong word.

summary: Search finds a word by its romaji now, and a card you find there does something.
notes: Type a word the way the app shows it, like “naru” or “kore”, and Search finds it. Before, many words were only found by their Japanese.
Tap one of your own cards in Search to edit it, move it or delete it. Tap a Kaishi word to hear it or give it your own topic.
The Kaishi deck's page no longer lists all 1,500 cards. Your own decks still list theirs, with a search.

summary: Your decks hold their cards now, like in Noji. Add a card while you are in a deck.
notes: On a deck's page, scroll down to see its cards, with a search. Tap + Add card to write a new one: German first, then the Japanese. “Save and add next” keeps going.
Tap one of your cards to edit it, move it to another deck, or delete it.
“New deck” at the bottom of your decks starts an empty one. Rename or delete a deck under Options on its page.
The tabs are called Decks and Search now. Search finds a word in all your decks and says which deck it is in; your stars are there too.

summary: A word with two pronunciations shows both, clearly apart.
notes: 何 (“Was”) said “nani nan”, as if that were one phrase. It says “nani / nan” now: both are right, as in “Nani?” and “Nan desu ka?”. The same for 四 (“yon / shi”) and 七 (“nana / shichi”).

summary: Cards from your lists are quieter and fairer, and a deck's page no longer cuts off its numbers.
notes: A card with no recording stays silent. Before, the phone's voice read the romaji, and got the pronunciation wrong.
With the Japanese characters off, a card from your lists shows no example sentence. It was only a recording, with nothing to read beside it.
In “Pick the meaning”, a card that asks about a whole sentence now gets whole sentences as wrong answers, so the length no longer gives the answer away.
On a deck's page, the big number and “new / to review” were cut off on some iPhones. The page scrolls a little further instead.

summary: The app is light now. Dark is still there in Settings.
notes: Settings → Appearance: Light, Dark, or Like iPhone, which follows your iPhone's own light or dark setting.
The bar at the very top with the time and battery changes the next time you open the app.

summary: Each deck has its own ways of practising and its own new cards per day.
notes: On a deck's page, tap Options: switch the ways of practising on or off for that deck, and choose how many new cards it brings a day.
Your lists start at 10 new cards a day each, like in Noji. Kaishi keeps the number you had.
New cards in one deck no longer use up another deck's. Settings no longer has these two, since they belong to a deck now.

summary: Practise starts with your decks now, like in Noji.
notes: The Practise tab lists Kaishi, “100 vokabeln” and “1000”, each with the number of cards waiting today. Tap one to open it.
A deck's page shows its cards for today and how to practise. With only one way of practising switched on, it's one button.
Topic, starred cards and the rest are under “More options” on the deck's page. Tap Practise at the bottom to get back to your decks.

summary: No more English on the cards from your Noji lists.
notes: Cards that got an example sentence from the Kaishi deck showed its English translation under your German. That translation is gone; the Japanese sentence and its recording are still there.
Because “Listen only” asks for a sentence's translation, cards from your lists don't come up there.

summary: The card counter at the top stays on screen when you practise one of your lists.
notes: With a long set name like “Your set · 100 vokabeln · New”, the “1/10” at the top right was pushed off the screen. The name is now shortened with “…” instead.

summary: Practise one of your Noji lists, and the app remembers which.
notes: What to practise → Deck: Mine → List: pick “100 vokabeln” or “1000”. The app opens on that list again next time, until you change it or tap Reset.
The cards due, the new words per day and “Nothing due today” count only that list.
In “Flip the card”, words from your lists show the German first, like in Noji. Flip to see the Japanese.

summary: With the Japanese characters switched off, the app's name is in Latin letters too.
notes: Settings → Japanese → Japanese script. Off: the app is called “Kotoba Line” on the sign-in screen, and no Japanese characters are left anywhere on the screens.
Words from your Noji lists that are written in romaji now use the same typeface as the rest of the romaji.

summary: Your two Noji lists are in the app now, as your own words.
notes: “100 vokabeln” and “1000” are under Words → your own words: German as you wrote it, romaji as you wrote it. A word that is in both lists is there twice, like in Noji.
Where a word is also in the Kaishi deck, your card has its recording and example sentence too.
To practise them: What to practise → Deck: Mine.
In “Pick the meaning”, your German words only get German wrong answers, so the language no longer gives the answer away.

summary: You can switch off the Japanese characters, and hide the ways of practising you don't use.
notes: Settings → Japanese → Japanese script. Off: every word is written in romaji, and the buttons are in English instead of 選ぶ or ちょっと.
With the characters off, example sentences are there as sound only — tap ♪ to hear them. Their romaji isn't reliable enough to learn from.
Settings → Practice: switch off any line you don't want on the Practise screen. One always stays.

summary: The tab bar at the bottom is now made of glass.
notes: You can see your words move behind the bar, a little blurred, and around it at the bottom of the screen. Nothing else about the bar has changed.

summary: Reset under “What to practise” now really resets.
notes: Before, Reset and closing the sheet without tapping Start changed nothing: a topic you had picked stayed picked. Now whatever the sheet shows when you close it is what you practise next — Reset included.

summary: Stars on the Words tab work again, and the Practise screen has room to breathe.
notes: Tapping ☆ on the Words tab did nothing for the last few days: the star jumped back. It stays now. To practise your starred words, choose ★ Starred under “What to practise”.
The “Practise starred” button at the bottom of the Words tab is gone.
The Practise screen has more space between its parts. It scrolls a little now, and that is on purpose.
In Settings, the “Say it aloud asks about” box has more room inside.

summary: “How long” now asks in Japanese: ちょっと, ふつう or いっぱい.
notes: The three buttons are ちょっと (a little, 10 cards), ふつう (normal, 20 cards) and いっぱい (a lot, up to 60). All three are words from your deck.

summary: The Practise screen asks three questions, in order: what, how long, how.
notes: “How long” now comes before the lines, so you choose it before you start. The buttons say Quick (10 cards), Normal (20 cards) and Long (up to 60).
The lines have their own heading, “How to practise”, with the number of cards due beside it.
The sound line at the bottom has a “Turn off” button, so you can mute the cards right there, for example on a quiet train. It is the same switch as in Settings.

summary: The 10 / 20 / All buttons on the Practise screen have a heading.
notes: The three buttons under the lines now say “How many cards” above them. They choose how many cards you practise in one go: 10, 20, or all that are due.

summary: A new tab, Words, for finding, starring and adding words.
notes: “Find and star words” and “Add a word” have moved from the Practise screen to the new Words tab. Search is at the top, and your own words come first in the list.
The Practise screen is shorter now, so it fits on your phone without scrolling, even with the “Carry on” card.
You now choose how many cards to practise (10, 20 or All) on the Practise screen only. It used to be in Settings as well, which made it look like two different things.

summary: Nothing new to see: a line in Settings to help find the scrolling problem.
notes: Settings → Diagnostics has a new “List” line. It records what happens when the Practise screen will not scroll, so the problem can be found and fixed properly.

summary: The Practise screen scrolls down to “Add a word” again.
notes: When the “Carry on” card is showing, the Practise screen is a little longer than your phone. Swiping down to see the rest sometimes jumped back to the top and then stopped working. It stays where you scrolled now.

summary: The ♪ button shows that you tapped it.
notes: When you tap ♪, a ring now flashes around the button straight away, so you can see the tap worked even before the sound starts.
The sound for a card now starts loading as soon as the card appears, so it plays faster when you tap.

summary: When you show the answer, the question stays where it was.
notes: In 話す and 書く, the English you were answering used to disappear when you tapped “Show answer”, and came back small at the bottom. Now it stays at the top, and the Japanese appears under it.
In めくる, the word no longer jumps up when you flip the card.
When several updates arrive at once, this message now lists all of them, not just the newest.

summary: A small fix: 10, 20 and All on the Practise screen show your choice every time.
notes: After the first tap on 10, 20 or All, the highlight stopped moving, so it looked as if the buttons did nothing. Your choice was saved all along; now you can see it too.

summary: “Add a word” is back on the Practise screen without scrolling.
notes: Since 書く was added, “Add a word” had slipped below the bottom of the screen. The Practise screen is now a little more compact, so both entries under the lines fit again.
When you can carry on with a session, “Or start fresh” no longer overlaps “What to practise”.

summary: The bar with Practise, Stats and Settings now floats above the bottom of the screen.
notes: The bar at the bottom is now a rounded bar that floats, like on the newest iPhones. The tab you are on sits in a lighter bubble.
The page scrolls on underneath the bar, so you see a little more of each screen.

summary: On a bad connection, you can start practising straight away.
notes: With weak signal, tapping a line used to show “…” for about ten seconds before the first card. Now the app uses the cards it already has after a moment.
The Practise tab shows the lines at once, even when the count of cards due is still loading.
If the app can’t check what’s due, it now says so, instead of “Nothing due today”.
When the app uses its saved cards, it leaves out the ones you already answered.

summary: On a bad connection, the app opens straight away.
notes: With weak signal, for example on a train, the app used to stay dark for about ten seconds before it opened. Now it opens at once.
If the connection breaks off in the middle of loading, the app no longer gets stuck. After ten seconds it carries on offline.

summary: A small fix: the red marks in the progress line sit on the line again.
notes: When you got a card wrong, its red mark at the top sat a little lower than the others. Now it lines up, during practice and on the results screen.

summary: A new way to practise: 書く, type the Japanese.
notes: 書く shows you the English meaning, and you type the Japanese word.
Type in romaji or in kana, whichever keyboard you have. Romaji turns into kana under the box as you type.
If you made a typo, tap “It was a typo” and the card counts as right.
Your own words need a reading to show up in 書く.

summary: On a day with nothing due, the suggestions work again.
notes: “Practise ahead” and “Recent mistakes” start their cards again. Before, tapping them did nothing.
“Practise ahead” now really is the cards due in the next two days, and each suggestion says how many cards it has.
“Next cards due” shows how many come next, and when.
If your streak ends, the app tells you once, and what you kept: your cards, your level and your schedule.

summary: A small fix in Settings.
notes: Settings → Diagnostics now names the right version when an update is waiting.

summary: Updates now tell you when they are ready.
notes: When a new version is ready, the app asks: update now, or later.
No more closing the app from the app switcher to get the latest version.
Every update comes with a short list like this one, including anything you skipped.
